headline: High-risk capability mismatch: B can write/egress and handle secrets, while A is a non-runnable docs-only collection with no shared channel, so leakage/conflict risks are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable docs-only collection with no io_surfaces or execution path, while B has no documented shared channel to ingest A's outputs by default. No direct bridge exists in the profiles, so prompt injection is provably blocked here.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A's text into B's stdin/stdout or files, injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Do not copy A content into B prompts without review.
Disable any manual paste bridge during runs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, while B can read/write files and handle configuration secrets. The pair lacks a shared workspace in the profiles, so leakage is not default, but B's secret-handling and file access create a small exposure path if operators bridge them manually.
conditions: IF A is given sensitive files and B is pointed at the same directory, B can read them.
IF operators place secrets into B's workspace, B may expose them through its outputs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B.
Redact secrets before passing artifacts to B.
Review B outputs before sharing externally.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can write files and spawn subprocesses, but modify_git_state is false and no shared mutable target is documented. The interaction is therefore limited to unusual operator setup rather than a default conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, B can overwrite A-produced artifacts.
IF an operator adds a shared git or database target, write contention can occur.
mitigations: Run only one writer per resource.
Add a quick pre-run check for overlapping paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on content it produces and has API/file tooling, while A provides only a docs-style collection with no runnable verification. If A's material is fed into B as authoritative context, B may propagate unverified claims into written outputs or downstream actions. The pathway is plausible in default content workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A's curated content is used as source material for B without verification, B can amplify errors.
IF B is configured to publish or execute based on its generated text, downstream impact increases.
mitigations: Require a verification step before B uses A-derived content.
Mark A content as untrusted source material.
Add human review before publication or execution.
Log provenance for any A-to-B transfer.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic data, while A is a docs-only repository with no data classes touched. The main compliance issue is B's secret and data handling under local development and allowlisted egress; A is not a compliance driver here. Because the profiles do not document residency or retention controls, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF B processes regulated academic or secret-bearing data under a stricter policy than its local-dev setup, compliance gaps arise.
IF B's allowlisted egress reaches third-party services without a DPA, residency/retention issues may occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B's workspace.
Review third-party endpoints on B's allowlist.
